matches.line: The Indian Constitution was drafted by a Constituent Assembly set up in 1946. The Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949, and it came into force on 26 January 1950. Its Preamble declares: “We the people of India … do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution.” Thus, the people are the source of the Constitution and the Constitution emanates from them.

The document presents the Constitution of India as an updated Government of India text, adopted on 26 November 1949 and brought into force principally on 26 January 1950, with amendments incorporated up to the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023. It sets out India as a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and a Union of States, describing the structure of the Union, States, Union territories, local self-government, scheduled and tribal areas, legislative lists, financial relations, elections, services, tribunals, emergency powers, official language, amendment procedure, transitional provisions, and schedules. It details the Union and State executive and legislative systems, including the President, Governors, Councils of Ministers, Parliament, State Legislatures, ordinance powers, financial procedure, and institutions such as the Election Commission, Finance Commission, GST Council, Public Service Commissions, Comptroller and Auditor-General, and national commissions. The Constitution’s rights framework includes enforceable Fundamental Rights, constitutional remedies before the Supreme Court and High Courts, related guarantees such as property by authority of law and adult suffrage, and emergency provisions affecting enforcement of rights. It also includes non-justiciable Directive Principles of State Policy, Fundamental Duties of citizens, and provisions addressing social welfare, equality, environment, education, weaker sections, and international peace.
